title: Legacy Archive Synthesis for Legal Discovery
business: Global law firms managing massive, multi-decade document repositories.
problem: Firms struggle with high costs and latency when performing discovery on legacy case files that require deep contextual understanding of outdated regulatory frameworks.
solution: Utilizing the 1M token context window of Claude Sonnet 5 allows firms to ingest entire case histories into a single prompt, leveraging its adaptive thinking to synthesize legal precedents without needing complex RAG architectures.
steps: Consolidate relevant case documents into a single serialized text stream.
Initialize the Claude API client using the claude-sonnet-5 model ID.
Inject the document stream into the message context, utilizing prompt caching to reduce recurring costs for frequently accessed archives.
Execute analytical queries using the high default effort setting to ensure deep reasoning on legacy data.
Retrieve synthesized legal summaries via the standard Messages API.
outcome: Reduced manual review time and improved consistency in identifying cross-case legal patterns.
limitation: The model has a knowledge cutoff of January 2026, meaning it cannot natively reason about regulatory changes or case law established after that date; developers must verify currency by checking the model's output against current legal databases.

code.content:
client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5", # Target legacy model ID
    max_tokens=4096,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Analyze these 500k words of case history..."}],
    extra_headers={"anthropic-beta": "output-300k-2026-03-24"} # Enable extended output for large summaries
)
